newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Petrol chain in court victory over Surgutneftegaz.
newsitem.headline: Petrol chain in court victory over Surgutneftegaz.

text.p: A petrol station chain which voted oil group NK Surgutneftegaz off its board and subsequently reduced Surgutneftegaz's shareholding said on Friday it had won a court case brought by Surgutneftegaz.

A lawyer for the AO Nefto-Kombi chain said a city arbitration court had rejected suits by Surgut Holding and its main operating subsidiary AO Surgutneftegaz to annul the results of a meeting of shareholders, which voted it off the board of directors.
"All decisions by the August 1996 shareholders meeting were ruled legitimate and Surgut's application was dismissed," Yevgeniya Mosheva told Reuters.
The deputy director of the northwest department of Surgutneftegaz, which had owned 42 percent of Nefto-Kombi, said his company would appeal the ruling, handed down on Monday.

The August 18 extraordinary shareholder meeting, called by shareholders who rent petrol stations from Nefto-Kombi, elected a new board of directors on which Surgut was not represented, the chain's director has said.
The chain later issued additional shares which lowered Surgutneftegaz's share of the company to 11 percent from 42 percent.
Nefto-Kombi has 105 gas stations in St Petersburg, of which 95 are are leased to 28 companies.
It had a net profit of 1.3 billion roubles in 1995.
Surgutneftegaz is one of Russia's largest oil production companies.
